newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine jobless excluding key province 17.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentine jobless excluding key province 17.3 pct.

text.p: Argentina's unemployment rate excluding the key province of Cordoba was 17.3 percent in October, the Indec statistics institute said Friday.

This should result in a nationwide joblessness rate somewhat higher than 17.3 percent, Indec Director Hector Montero told reporters. "Historically, unemployment in Cordoba is higher than the national average," he said.
Unemployment is measured twice a year. In the last reading taken in May it stood at 17.1 percent, whereas in October 1995 it hit a record 18.4 percent.
Figures for Cordoba, and therefore a final natiowide count, are expected sometime next week.

In the May 1995-October 1996 period 199,000 new jobs were created, but demand grew by 202,000, resulting in a 3,000 jobs deficit, said Carlos Rodriguez, chief adviser to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez.
Unemployment, the Achilles heel of Argentina's otherwise successful economic stabilization plan, is expected to drop between two and five percentage points next year, Rodriguez said.
Underemployment -- those working in part-time or temporary jobs -- was put at 13.6 percent by October.

The government was originally due to release the unemployment figure next Thursday. Although it gave no reason for issuing incomplete data earlier than expected, figures started leaking to the press this week and the local media started speculating with a possible early release.
Fernandez said recently that a robust 6.6 percent economic growth in the third quarter was a reason to be optimistic about Argentina's economic prospects.
